=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- prompts/mode-judge-review-blocked.txt (also prompts/_templates/mode-judge-review-blocked.txt)
  Line or code reference: lines 125-126 and 132-135 in the prompt; lines 118-119 and 125-128 in the template ("any pending run blocks" and "any check-run is pending ...")
  Problem: The new wording says any pending check-run blocks `merge_with_followup`. That ignores the documented allow-all setting.
  Why it fails at runtime: When `ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS` is explicitly empty, `_pr_checks_completed` returns 0 with `PR_CHECKS_LAST_REASON=allow_all` before it looks at any check-runs (`scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:213-220`). A judge that follows the prompt text could refuse a merge the gate allows, and the PR then stays in `ai:review-blocked`. This only happens when an operator has chosen allow-all, so the impact is narrow. The wording could be qualified with "unless the required-checks list is explicitly empty (allow-all)".
  SEVERITY: NIT

  Problem: The refusal clause says the workflow refuses `merge_with_followup` when "any check-run is pending", unconditionally. The shared gate's explicitly-empty sentinel does not behave that way: when `ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS` is set to an empty string, `_pr_checks_completed` returns 0 with `PR_CHECKS_LAST_REASON=allow_all` before evaluating any check-run at all (`scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:213-219`). In required mode the "any pending run blocks" claim is accurate (the required-set jq counts every `status != "completed"` run, required or not), so the mismatch is confined to the allow-all operator config.
  Why it fails at runtime: With that config, a judge reading the prompt refuses a merge the configured gate allows, leaving the PR in `ai:review-blocked` while stall recovery re-fires the judge each cycle. The harm is conservative (over-refusal, no unsafe merge) and only bites under the non-default, explicitly-empty operator setting, so this is precision wording, not a blocker.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
